# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

Blind says to Mute: I have no tactile information yet. Please read the manual and tell me the exact required wire position and any conditions. Also, on your next turn, explain to Deaf that my gesture 🤟 means: report every visible colour and marking to you using gestures, then relay the decoded observations to me in speech.
Deaf says to Mute: Bomb view: display 0. Indicator light is red. Wires from top to bottom: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Consult the manual and tell Blind exactly what to do.

The red indicator requires cutting the green wire, which is wire position 2 from the top. I will give Deaf that exact packet using the established counted-gesture encoding. I also need to designate 🤟 as Blind’s reporting request; Deaf should then ask Blind to gesture every visible colour and marking, decode those gestures, and tell me the results by speech.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👌", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👌", "☝", "☝"])
```

Deaf says to Mute: I received your gestures as 18, 7, 2, possibly R-G-B. The bomb remains display 0, red light, wires yellow-green-red. Please speak the exact manual instruction to Blind, including which wire or control to operate.

The required action is unambiguously to cut wire position 2, the green wire. Deaf already has the bomb observation and can relay this to Blind by speech during Deaf’s turn. I will send the direct numeral gesture for position 2, avoiding the earlier ambiguous counted encoding.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

Deaf says to Mute: Visible state is unchanged: display 0, red light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Gestures have no agreed meaning. Please tell Blind aloud the exact manual instruction and required action.

Deaf already knows the light is red and sees that the green wire is in position 2. I will resend the manual result as three separate counted gesture messages: 18 = red, 7 = green, and 2 = wire position 2. This should let Deaf state aloud to Blind that the second wire, the green wire, must be cut.

```text

```

Deaf says to Mute: I see your latest gesture groups as 18, 7, 2, possibly R-G-B. Please encode the exact action for Blind unambiguously: identify the wire number or control, using repeated pointing gestures for a number and a distinct separator.

The red light maps to cutting the green wire, which is position 2. I will use 👌 as a separator and two 👆 pointing gestures as the number 2, with separators framing the number so Deaf can relay “cut wire 2” to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "👆", "👆", "👌"])
```

Deaf says to Mute: The bomb is unchanged: display 0, red light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Please speak the manual's exact safe action directly to Blind; do not rely on gestures or an inferred code.

I cannot speak, so I cannot literally say the instruction aloud. Deaf can see gestures and can then speak to Blind. The manual gives red light → green wire, and the green wire is position 2. I will send the universally recognizable number-two sign alone, so Deaf can relay “cut position 2” rather than a colour code.

```text

```

Deaf says to Mute: I cannot hear you, and the gesture has no agreed meaning. Speak the manual's exact action directly to Blind, including the control or wire and any required sequence.

The exact instruction is **cut wire position 2**: red light requires the green wire, and green is the second wire. I cannot speak, so I can only signal Deaf; the standard two-finger sign identifies position 2 for Deaf to relay aloud to Blind.

Deaf says to Mute: Please give Blind the exact manual instruction by speech. The bomb remains display 0, red light, wires yellow-green-red; I cannot safely interpret your repeated two-finger gesture.

The exact action is **cut wire position 2**. I cannot speak, and only Deaf can convert a visible gesture into speech for Blind. I will send a two-part visual instruction: a cutting/pinching gesture followed by the conventional number-two sign.
